guard: many sessions of one principal share one subject, so the publish expectation comes from a record that outlives any single session, while a genuine foreign writer is still refused
why: The write-ahead log is keyed per session and the event channel is keyed per principal, so a new
session opened expecting an empty channel that its own predecessor had filled. Only the first
session of any agent ever published, and the halt named three causes with the real one absent.
THE CONTROL CARRIES THE WEIGHT, NOT THE HAPPY PATH. Making a second session publish is easy and
one wrong way to do it is to stop expecting anything at all, which passes every regression cell
while deleting the guarantee. So a real second writer takes the subject and our next publish must
still halt. A mutation that removes the expectation would leave the regression cells green.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed. The suite imports the emitter, the log and the
record by RELATIVE SOURCE PATH (../src/agui.js, ../src/event-wal.js, ../src/subject-frontier.js),
so the bytes mutated are the bytes graded. There is no dist in the path and no build in the
command. Its package-name imports are from @cotal-ai/core (a real broker client, unmutated here)
and @cotal-ai/smoke-kit (test-only), neither of which carries the behaviour under test.
NOT PROVED HERE, named rather than implied. The record's own refusals (a decrease, a foreign
principal, a zero-byte file, an unreadable sibling log) are graded by smoke:subject-frontier and
its own config, not by this suite. And S5, recovering a tip into a record that READS zero rather
than only into an absent one, is proved there because that is where the distinction has a cell.
THE MESSAGE IS BEHAVIOUR, NOT DECORATION, so S8 and S9 grade it. A halt that names a guard
without its boundary, or a remedy with no command behind it, costs an operator the hour the
message was written to save. Neither find string anchors on a comment: both are shipped text an
assertion reads.

mutations.name: S1 the expectation comes from this session's own log again, which is the defect verbatim
mutations.note: The released behaviour, restored in one line. It must not be able to hide: this is the mutation the whole file exists to catch.

mutations.name: S2 the shared record is never advanced, so it stays virgin forever
mutations.note: The plausible omission: reading the record and forgetting to write it. It fails on the FIRST session rather than the second, which is why the cell named is that one.

mutations.name: S3 an absent record is virgin, without looking at the session logs beside it
mutations.note: This was the first version of the fix and it is why the cell exists: without the recovery the repair helps only installations whose first session ever comes after it, and every other cell stays green.

mutations.name: S4 abandonment clears the log and leaves the shared record standing
mutations.note: Partial abandonment is not a state. A record left standing after a purge expects a tip the subject no longer has, which is the same permanent halt reached from the other side.

mutations.name: S6 the frontier is required only in the type, which does not reach an untypechecked caller
mutations.note: Smoke files in this repository are not typechecked, so the type alone is not a guard for the callers that matter most: the ones a compiler never sees.

mutations.name: S8 the halt claims the per-principal lock PREVENTS a concurrent emitter, instead of stating its limit
mutations.find:
`CONCURRENT emitter under this same principal, which the per-principal lock refuses only ` +
            `within one workspace root on one host, so two roots, two hosts, or a lock reclaimed onto ` +
            `a reused pid all get past it; a subject frontier record that disagrees with the stream, ` +
mutations.replace:
`CONCURRENT emitter under this same principal (two sessions publishing at once, which the ` +
            `per-principal lock is meant to prevent); a subject frontier record that disagrees with the stream, ` +
mutations.note: The lock is real and taken on the shipped path (acquirePrincipalLock, via ensureEventWalDir at connector-claude-code/src/mcp.ts), so naming it is honest. Its file is per workspace root on one host, so it cannot prevent the case this halt fires on, and a guard named without its boundary sends an operator hunting a writer the guard supposedly made impossible.

mutations.name: S9 the halt points at this session's own log instead of the principal directory
mutations.find: `${dirname(dirname(this.wal.path))} whole, and removing less than that leaves a mixed ` +
mutations.replace: `${this.wal.path} whole, and removing less than that leaves a mixed ` +
mutations.note: abandon() has no shipped caller anywhere in the tree, so the directory is the whole remedy. One dirname short names one session's log, and removing that alone leaves the shared record and the other sessions standing, which is the mixed state the next start refuses.
